messages:
emma: FYI, brought up a new HF chat_template -> Redwood conversion and the assistant outputs are getting truncated / weird stop tokens. anyone seen this pattern before?
raj: can you paste the exact jinja snippet you converted?
emma: here it is (minimal):
```
{% for m in messages %}{{ m.role }}: {{ m.content }}
{% endfor %}
```
emma: we were expecting Redwood to wrap roles like `<|system|>` etc but output has leftover jinja whitespace and sometimes flattened role markers into a single token.
marco: quick diagnosis: sounds like special tokens not being registered in the tokenizer config.json. if the model uses sentinel tokens like `<|system|>`/`<|assistant|>` but tokenizer doesn't treat them as atomics, they can split into sub-tokens and break stop-sequence matching.
sarah: concrete repro?
emma: run on v2 of the model we onboarded — tokenizer config had only `bos_token` and `eos_token`, no `additional_special_tokens`. conversion script naively replaced role templates with plain text, e.g. `SYSTEM:` instead of preserving HF sentinels. Redwood's prompt formatter expects explicit stop sequences or role markers as individual tokens.
raj: show what Redwood ended up sending to the runtime (sanitized):
```
SYSTEM: You are a helpful assistant.
USER: What is the capital of France?
ASSISTANT:
```
raj: but model's tokenizer actually produces tokens like `['<', '|', 'system', '|', '>']` when special token not registered. stop=["<|assistant|>"] then never matches.
emma: exact failure: responses truncated when we set `stop=["ASSISTANT:"]` because the real emitted tokens didn't match.
marco: fix is twofold: 1) make conversion preserve HF sentinel tokens in template (literal `<|user|>`), or 2) add those as special tokens in tokenizer before generation.
sarah: example patch we used locally:
```
# python/hf conversion helper
tokenizer.add_special_tokens({
  "additional_special_tokens": ["<|system|>", "<|user|>", "<|assistant|>"]
})
model.resize_token_embeddings(len(tokenizer))
```
marco: also check config.json mapping: set `bos_token` to `<|system|>` if HF model expects it at start, or at least set `eos_token` consistently. some quantized checkpoints we tested lost `tokenizer.json` so those defaults were missing.
emma: we also saw a quirk with quantization: when using 4-bit gptq variants the first tokenization call returns a different length (off by 1) compared to fp16 — suspected padding token index mismatch causing KV cache offsets.
raj: oof. did that cause coherency/regression in evals?
emma: yes — our eval harness (small HELM-ish suite) showed ~7% drop on instruction-following and some hallucination spikes when switching to gptq_4bit without re-registering special tokens.
sarah: TL;DR checklist for conversion:
- preserve literal sentinels in Jinja -> don't replace with plain `SYSTEM:` text
- ensure tokenizer has `additional_special_tokens` for all sentinels
- align `bos_token`/`eos_token`/`pad_token` in config.json with tokenizer
- run small tokenization parity test across fp16 and quant variants (compare token ids and lengths)
- add stop sequences at runtime using exact sentinel tokens rather than human-readable labels
marco: small token parity test snippet we added to CI:
```
def parity(tokens, tokenizer):
    enc = tokenizer(tokens, add_special_tokens=False)
    return enc.input_ids, len(enc.input_ids)

# compare
fp_ids, fp_len = parity(example_text, fp16_tokenizer)
q_ids, q_len = parity(example_text, q_tokenizer)
assert fp_ids == q_ids, "token ids differ"
```
raj: also watch out for role order and trailing newlines — HF chat templates sometimes put system at the end of the jinja loop which we accidentally kept; Redwood expects system first. small reordering bug can flip semantics.
emma: resolved for this model by: preserving `<|system|>` sentinel in the template, registering special tokens, and adding an automated tokenization parity check in onboarding. latency regressed minimally with the extra tokens but correctness returned.
tokenizer-bot: note: added job `token-parity-check` to eng-ml CI for new-models. see pipeline #342. :white_check_mark:
raj: great, can you open a PR with the conversion helpers and the new test?
emma: will do this afternoon. tagging @sarah for docs update on the conversion guide. :memo:
sarah: got it, I'll add a short how-to and example snippets to the onboarding doc.
marco: leaving a note — if anyone sees weird truncation after quantizing, prioritize token parity & special tokens before blaming kernels. :slightly_smiling_face:
